one_liner: Senior executive-level manager planning how the federal Judiciary takes over its buildings and leases from GSA, covering org design, workforce, budgets, contracting and transition plans.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship skills and IEM consulting background give some relevance to briefings, stakeholder coordination and change work. However, the posting requires one full year of specialized experience in ALL four areas, including real property acquisitions, leasing, and FAR/contracting officer roles. At $169K-$210K, this is a senior role that typically expects 5-10+ years in facilities and real property, which nothing on file suggests Daniel has.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public, fed-competitive, fed-excepted), so no prior federal status is needed.

You need at least 52 weeks of specialized experience covering ALL of these areas: organizational change management (workforce analysis, org design, risk and cost/benefit), senior-executive analysis and briefings, real property acquisitions and leasing, and contracting/FAR/COR roles.
No education requirement and no security clearance are required.
Before starting, you must pass an FBI fingerprint check, a public trust suitability check and E-Verify, and complete a trial period.
Mandatory narrative responses are required, and missing them results in not receiving full consideration.
strategy: Before applying, check honestly whether your IEM work included real property, leasing, building services procurement and FAR-based contracting. If it did not, skip this posting rather than overstate your experience, since self-ratings are verified against your resume.

If you did support government clients on contracts, describe the specifics in your resume: your role relative to the CO/COR, the contract vehicles used, and any task orders or deliverables you managed.
Frame your IEM consulting as change management and decision support for government leaders: briefings, reports, stakeholder working groups and risk analysis, only where these are accurate.
Keep the resume to two pages, list hours per week and month/year dates, and mirror the four specialized experience areas nearly word-for-word.
Draft the mandatory narratives early with concrete examples, then submit before the November 3, 2026 close.
For realistic targets, look at FEMA, state VDEM, or Prince William County emergency management analyst roles, or legislative staff roles that fit your policy strengths.
resume_bullets: Led [number] working groups of [stakeholders/agencies] for [government client], preparing agendas, schedules and communications to support [project/initiative].
Developed written analyses and briefings for [senior official title] on [topic], including risk and cost/benefit options that informed [decision].
Supported contract deliverables under [contract type/vehicle] by coordinating with the client's COR on [scope, schedule, invoicing], in accordance with [FAR/agency guidance].
interview_questions: Describe an organizational change initiative you oversaw, including how you assessed workforce needs and risks.
How would you approach planning the transfer of building custody and leases from GSA to the Judiciary?
Explain the roles of contracting officers and CORs, and give an example of how you worked with them.
Tell us about a high-stakes briefing you delivered to executives and how you shaped the message.
watch_outs: The specialized experience requirements in real property and federal acquisitions are strict, and Daniel likely lacks them.
The salary level signals senior candidates with 5-10+ years in facilities, so competition will be stiff.
Overrating yourself on the questionnaire will be caught when ratings are checked against your resume and lowered to match.
The role is based in DC (telework eligible but not remote), which means a commute from Manassas, and it includes about 5% travel.
